title: Anker Nebula Cosmos projector, model D2140 (device D2140-Cosmos, SDMC board, Amlogic/droidlogic,
notes:
Anker Nebula Cosmos projector, model D2140 (device D2140-Cosmos, SDMC board, Amlogic/droidlogic,
armeabi-v7a, 2 GB RAM, 4 GB /data), Android TV 9 (SDK 28), build PI.20240530. Vietnam.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/disable.sh examples/anker-nebula-d2140/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/restore.sh examples/anker-nebula-d2140/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (HOME priority 2, ~190 MB RAM). Only other HOME claimant is
com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. Default IME is already Gboard.
Remote global keys (keycodes 2000+) go to com.sdmc.GlobalKey (dumpsys window policy, mKeyMapping).
HDMI 1 and 2 come from com.droidlogic.tvinput, so the launcher's Inputs pill lists them.
/data was 90% full (411 MB free) out of the box; `pm trim-caches 999G` frees the app caches.
Netflix: Play Store says "not compatible". The set has no ro.nrdp.* properties, so it is not Netflix
certified; the TV app (com.netflix.ninja) does not run. A certified stick on HDMI is the way round it.

DO NOT DISABLE on this model (projector hardware, inputs, remote):
com.droidlogic.*                      # SoC services, HDMI inputs, Live TV, subtitles, OTA
com.droidlogic.keystone               # keystone (picture shape) correction
com.sdmc.GlobalKey                    # remote global keys
com.sdmc.bluetoothconnect             # Bluetooth remote pairing wizard
com.sdmc.bluetoothspeaker             # Bluetooth speaker mode
com.sdmc.oemprovisionservice          # OEM provisioning
com.oceanwing.receiver                # remote control, Nebula IME, screen control
com.oceanwing.nebulalinker            # Nebula Connect phone app, device info, update dispatch
com.oceanwing.ota                     # firmware updates (kept by owner's choice)
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith  # owns the Wi-Fi saved during setup
Left alone, purpose unclear: com.sdmc.leakbackcustomer, com.sdmc.cleardataservice
